claims.text: An actively learned moment tensor potential trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations near the melting temperature will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The MTP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 40–50% relative to conventional EAM references.
Equimolar Ta–Cr–V is a representative refractory high-entropy-alloy system to which the proposed method applies.
The relevant initial states include both solid and liquid phases near the melting point.
The conventional EAM reference in TOR-TILD should be replaced by an actively learned MTP trained incrementally on ab initio configurations from both phases.
The proposed simulations apply at approximately 2000–2500 K.
The liquid exhibits extensive configurational variation under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
MTP many-body descriptors can represent bond lengths, bond angles, and higher-order correlations in the solid and liquid.
On-the-fly adaptive training enables the MTP to capture diverse local atomic environments.
Continuous active learning from ab initio data allows the MTP to adapt to diverse local configurations.
Representing more diverse local configurations enhances reference–target phase-space overlap.
Enhanced phase-space overlap shortens the thermodynamic-integration path and reduces discrepancies between computed and target free-energy profiles.
The proposed MTP will yield an absolute free-energy improvement of approximately 30–50 meV/atom relative to EAM when benchmarked against direct ab initio calculations.
Conventional EAM references used in TOR-TILD have limited ability to represent the configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid.
The method is applicable across refractory multicomponent high-entropy alloys such as equimolar Ta–Cr–V.
A parallel comparison of MTP and EAM references at 2000, 2250, and 2500 K can test the predicted improvement.
Failure to obtain either the predicted 40–50% mismatch reduction or a 30–50 meV/atom error reduction relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of active-learning convergence across the relevant configuration space would falsify the hypothesis.
